sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date for the maamar for Purim 5744.

translations.translation: B'Siyata D'Shmaya.
Purim 5744*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the essence of the miracle was the king's sleep being disturbed, as interpreted by the Rebbe and the Maharil.

translations.translation: "On that night, the king's sleep was disturbed,"
and the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, brings in his maamar beginning with the word "Zeh,"
that it is stated in the Minhagei Maharil
that from "on that night" one must raise his voice in its reading, because this is the essence of the miracle
[for "on that night" is the beginning of the intensity of the miracle].
And he makes a precise point about this,
that at first glance the essence of the miracle was Esther's request and her supplications, "for we have been sold, I and my people,"
[and also the preparations she made beforehand,
"Go, gather all the Jews... and fast for me"],
yet here it says that the essence and intensity of the miracle is that the king's sleep was disturbed.
And he brings on this,
that it is stated in the Yalkut,
"On that night, the king's sleep was disturbed" — this is the King of the World,
and is there sleep before Him?
Rather, when Israel sins, He makes Himself as if asleep,
and when they do His will, [He does] not,
"He neither slumbers nor sleeps."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the disturbance of the King's sleep is the essence of the miracle, because exile is a time of sleep, and the miracle was that this sleep was shaken off.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that behold, man is a "likeness of the Supernal,"
and therefore all the matters above are in the same manner as they are in man
("You are called 'man'"),
"above, corresponding to the pattern below,"
and in the language of the verse,
"As water reflects a face back to a face, so the heart of man to man,"
and therefore,
when Israel are in a state of sleep,
meaning that the matters of Torah and Mitzvos
(through which they are a "likeness of the Supernal")
are in a state of sleep for them,
through this, sleep is caused, as it were, also in the King of the World.
And as it is written,
"I am asleep," and it is stated in the Zohar
"in exile,"
that from the side of the sleep of Israel during the time of exile,
through this, sleep is caused, as it were, also above.
And this is that "on that night the king's sleep was disturbed" is the intensity of the miracle,
because according to the order of the chain of descent,
the time of exile is a time of sleep
(above),
and that "on that night"
(exile)
"the king's sleep was disturbed" — the King of the World — this is the intensity of the miracle.
And this is also the precise meaning of the expression "the king's sleep was disturbed"
(specifically "was disturbed"),
for the expression "the king's sleep was disturbed"
(that sleep was disturbed from the king)
indicates that it was fitting for sleep to be upon the king
[similar to what is said about a person who was disturbed from his place],
because the time of exile is a time of sleep
(as above),
except that there was a miracle that the sleep was disturbed from Him.
